base-acea-hwsd_upper_layer_texture: HWSD v2.0 upper-layer (0–20 or 20–40 cm) texture (sand, clay) of one soil component, not necessarily the dominant one, read from the ~1 km pixel at each 0.5° cell centre and applied to the whole profile
base-acea-list-isda_s3: iSDA Africa soil properties, top-layer sand and clay only (applied to the whole profile), read at each cell centre, one per 0.5° cell, assigned by list order, not by location, so a cell's soil can come from elsewhere in the region
base-acea-list-isda: iSDA Africa topsoil properties, top-layer sand and clay only (applied to the whole profile), read at each cell centre, one per 0.5° cell, assigned by list order, not by location, so a cell's soil can come from elsewhere in the region
base-acea-list-hwsd: HWSD v2.0 dominant soil component (max share), top-layer sand and clay only (applied to the whole profile), read at each cell centre, one per 0.5° cell, assigned by list order, not by location, so a cell's soil can come from elsewhere in the region
base-acea-list-placeholder: a generic placeholder soil profile (no soil data was retrieved), one per 0.5° cell, assigned by list order, not by location, so a cell's soil can come from elsewhere in the region
base-acea-default_values: A generic default soil for every cell (sand 40%, clay 25%); no HWSD value was available
base-acea-engine_installed: No soil in this package; ACEA reads the soil file installed with the engine
base-sarra: SARRA-Py's bundled Africa soil data, read by the engine and not carried in this package: root-zone depth from a GYGA rootable-depth map; soil water capacity, surface-layer thickness, initial deep-soil water and runoff from iSDA soil classes at TAMSAT resolution via an HWSD-derived class table (versions not recorded). The package's parameters/soil.yaml is loaded, but the SARRA-Py version the runner pins (ac769ea) uses none of its values
ptf-3of12: ; water limits estimated with a pedotransfer function adapted from Saxton & Rawls (2006) for 3 of 12 layers
ptf-1of12: ; water limits estimated with a pedotransfer function adapted from Saxton & Rawls (2006) for 1 of 12 layers
shallow-1of1-20: ; 1 of 1 profiles is shallower than 100 cm (depth 20 cm)
shallow-1of2-20: ; 1 of 2 profiles is shallower than 100 cm (depth 20 cm)
shallow-3of40-40: ; 3 of 40 profiles are shallower than 100 cm (depth 40 cm)
shallow-2of2-20_50: ; 2 of 2 profiles are shallower than 100 cm (depths 20 to 50 cm)
noprof-3of10: ; 3 of 10 grid cells have no soil profile in the package
noprof-1of10: ; 1 of 10 grid cells has no soil profile in the package
over-4: ; user soil overrides applied to the top layer of 4 cells
over-1: ; user soil overrides applied to the top layer of 1 cell
chem-3_3_3: ; chemistry defaults used (bulk density 1.40 g/cm³ ×3, organic carbon 0.50 % ×3, pH 6.5 ×3)
organd-2_1: ; 2 organic and 1 andic layers (of 12 layers in 3 profiles; 5 cells), outside the pedotransfer function's calibration range
organd-1_0: ; 1 organic layer (of 4 layers in 1 profile; 1 cell), outside the pedotransfer function's calibration range
organd-0_3: ; 3 andic layers (of 12 layers in 3 profiles; 2 cells), outside the pedotransfer function's calibration range
acea-default-2of20: ; 2 of 20 cells use a generic default soil (sand 40%, clay 25%)
acea-default-1of20: ; 1 of 20 cells uses a generic default soil (sand 40%, clay 25%)
acea-skip-3of20: ; 3 of 20 cells have no soil value and are skipped by the engine
acea-skip-1of20: ; 1 of 20 cells has no soil value and is skipped by the engine
acea-field-2of20: ; 2 of 20 cells lacked sand or clay and use the default for it
acea-field-1of20: ; 1 of 20 cells lacked sand or clay and uses the default for it
